title: The BRICS+: rebels without a common cause
gist: After the 2026 New Delhi summit, Ved Shinde argues the enlarged BRICS+ (about 45% of world population, 35% of GDP, 30% of oil) is pulled three ways: China uses it for renminbi internationalisation and leverage over Trump, Russia wants an anti-Western coalition and a hedge against Beijing, and India participates mainly to block China and hedge against an erratic Washington. Intra-member feuds make it a 'diplomatic sociability' club rather than a coherent bloc.

themes.theme: Formidable on paper, incoherent in practice

insights.claim: The enlarged BRICS+ covers around 45% of global population, about 35% of global GDP and about 30% of the world's oil, but the author argues these aggregate numbers overstate its real power.

themes.theme: Origins in resentment of the G8

insights.claim: BRICS grew out of Jim O’Neill's 2001 'BRICs' label and gained momentum after the Global Financial Crisis undermined the legitimacy of the Western-led economic order and emerging powers resented G8 rule-setting.
insights.speaker: Ved Shinde
insights.so_what: Financial crises in the West tend to accelerate non-Western institution-building.
